q: Which of these is NOT produced during design development?
n: Technical/material specifications are typically finalized during the contract documents phase, while roof plans, ceiling plans, and floor plans are developed and refined earlier, in design development (Source: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004), IRR – Scope of Architectural Practice (design phases)).
scenario:
A landowner plans to convert a rectangular, R-1-classified parcel totaling 1,934.72 square meters into an open-market residential subdivision within a built-up urban district. The plan calls for six exclusive, semi-upscale housing units, each on a 132.00-square-meter lot allocation, with each unit's enclosed floor space — its total gross floor area — capped at 77.00 square meters (counting only the roofed, enclosed portions, excluding any floor area the owner might add later). Each house lot runs 12 meters deep.

The parcel is an interior lot (not a corner lot) with a 32.00-meter-wide frontage facing east. The ground falls evenly at a 1% grade along its length, draining south. A 15.00-meter-wide road right-of-way fronts the property at 0.00 elevation, flanked on both sides by a 1.80-meter paver-block sidewalk.

An 8.00-meter-wide interior cluster street cuts through the middle of the site along its long axis, meeting the main right-of-way at a perpendicular intersection. This interior street climbs at a 10% grade running west to east and provides direct frontage to all ten house lots, five on each side. The two outermost lots at the street's western end are each 31.45% wider than the lot at the center of the row.

Four objectives guide the design: stay within R-1 zoning parameters; produce a tightly planned residential enclave that can serve as a model development for the area; maximize the owner's financial return; and give the project a distinctive, landmark-quality presence.

q: In an R-1 development, which sides of a lot may carry firewalls?
n: R-1 developments consist of single-detached houses, which by definition are freestanding with open space on all sides, so firewalls — shared party walls between adjoining units — do not apply.
